title: Niacinamide
caption: Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 that works inside the skin cell, not just on the surface. It helps regulate how much oil your sebaceous glands produce, reinforces the proteins that hold your skin barrier together, and interrupts the chain of events that sends pigment to the surface — which is why you'll see it in products marketed for pores, oiliness, and dark spots alike. It's not a treatment for any one condition; it's a support ingredient that makes the skin's own processes run more steadily. Knowing that helps you read an ingredient label instead of just a marketing claim. Not medical advice, just the honest basics. Learn more at cliniclick.ae
